angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 526,645 km at 111.53 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.9659 +/- 0.0266 mas (same row, RUWE 1.40): 111.53 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.757 +/- 0.035 solar radii from Hedges et al. 2019, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-198 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...880L...5H/abstract): 526,645 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.799 +/- 0.091 solar masses from Hedges et al. 2019, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-198 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...880L...5H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5212.9 +/- 99 K from Hedges et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-198 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...880L...5H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hedges et al. 2019, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-198 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019ApJ...880L...5H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-198.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.582, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, K2-198: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-198 (pscomppars): [M/H] 0.094 dex, from Pope et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.461.3399P/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-198 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.40084, from Pope et al. 2016 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016MNRAS.461.3399P/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 3628687065162340224, flags_flame 00: age_flame 1.1300575 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 0.2 to 2.676356)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/635/A43/table2 (Stellar rotation periods from K2 Campaigns 0-18), column Prot: 7.18 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/635/A43/table2 (Stellar rotation periods from K2 Campaigns 0-18), column Prot: 7.18 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, K2-198: projected rotation speed 5.4 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2025A&A...697A.102T)
rotationPeriodMeasuredSource: Measured in this project from the K2 mission's own light curves of campaigns 6 and 17 (packages/telescope-cli/src/archives/tess/reduce.mts), by the method and criteria of Reinhold & Hekker (2020, A&A 635, A43): 7.04 d, the mean of the campaigns' 7.02 and 7.06 d, the light swinging by 2.4% as the star turns

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
